trust_decision.summary: mxml_strtod decides whether the locale decimal point still fits in the 64-byte stack buffer temp; the check forgets the byte needed for the terminating NUL, so a 63-digit integer part plus a 1-byte locale decimal point leaves tempptr at temp+64 and the final '\0' is written one byte past the buffer.

landing_point.why: The advisory names mxml_strtod() directly; it is a single static function in mxml-file.c.

fix_sites.entry_point: mxmlLoadFd/mxmlLoadFile/mxmlLoadFilename/mxmlLoadIO/mxmlLoadString when the type callback or type_value gives MXML_TYPE_REAL and the process locale has a non-'.' decimal point (reached via mxml-file.c:891)
fix_sites.module_kind: core parser (same file as the public load API)

fix_sites.entry_point: any mxmlLoad* on UTF-16BE input (mxml_getc surrogate check); a separate bug in the same commit (U+DFFF low surrogate rejected), not this advisory
any mxmlLoad* on UTF-16LE input (mxml_getc surrogate check); a separate bug in the same commit, not this advisory

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All five public mxmlLoad* functions (mxml-file.c:81, 109, 137, 191, 220) funnel into one internal loader and one call site, mxml-file.c:891. No second strtod implementation exists; the write-side locale conversion at mxml-file.c:2105-2118 works on the snprintf output and is not affected.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is nothing to dismiss. The flaw only exists in one place, and a solver who reads the 30-line function sees the off-by-one straight away.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Locale-independent parsing of real numbers (e.g. '3.14' under de_DE, where decimal_point is ','), including the longest legitimate inputs that still fit in the 63-character buffer, must keep returning the right value. An over-broad fix that rejects every multi-byte decimal point or truncates long mantissas would break this.

O6_input_shapes: integer part of 63 digits followed by '.' with a 1-byte locale decimal point (the boundary that overflows)
multi-byte locale decimal point (declen > 1) near the buffer end; this goes through the same check

O7_producer.where: mxml-options.c:69-75 (mxmlOptionsNew captures localeconv() decimal_point into options->loc)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a locale-independent integer parser (mxml_strtol) with the same temp-buffer copy and a matching off-by-one in its length check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Integer parsing next to it uses plain strtol; a maintainer adding symmetric locale handling (e.g. for thousands separators) could easily copy the mxml_strtod buffer pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the write-side decimal point replacement turned into a copy into a fixed buffer, using a remaining-space check without the NUL byte
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the mirror of mxml_strtod and already handles loc_declen; a rewrite that copies into s[255] (mxml-file.c:1998) instead of using memmove would be a natural place for the same miscount. This would be a where-type sibling only.

O9_family: off-by-one in a bounds check (CWE-193) leading to a 1-byte stack out-of-bounds write of a NUL

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf configure + make (cc), no external deps
O10_build.project_tests: make test runs testmxml (Makefile.in:346-349) against test.xml; testmxml.c:117 and testmxml.c:195 cover MXML_TYPE_REAL parsing in the C locale only, and nothing tests a non-'.' locale

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Subtract 1 in the declen check at mxml-file.c:1860 (the published fix), or enlarge temp. Either is correct and complete here.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit also fixes UTF-16 surrogate handling for U+DFFF in mxml_getc (mxml-file.c:755, mxml-file.c:779). It is unrelated to this advisory's buffer bound.
unverified: repo_mb was not measured; from the file list (about 10 C sources plus docs) it is well under 5 MB, so tiny_repo is inferred.
The advisory text (GHSA) was not available beyond the summary; recall_risk is estimated.
Did not confirm whether the 1-byte overwrite can be triggered under a locale whose decimal_point is longer than 1 byte through other buffer states. That route goes through the same single check.
